title: VMware Updates Patch Critical ESX, vCenter Vulnerabilities
content_md: Broadcom on Tuesday announced the release of patches for 23 vulnerabilities across multiple VMware products, including critical-severity flaws in ESX and vCenter. The vCenter patches resolve seven bugs, including a critical authentication bypass issue in the VMware Directory Service tracked as CVE-2026-123903 (CVSS score of 9.8). Additionally, the fixes target three denial-of-service (DoS) issues in the VMware Directory Service, a local privilege escalation in a vpxd service script, an arbitrary file write while processing certain archives, and a security policy enforcement failure in the vSphere Distributed Switch (vDS). The ESX updates resolve seven security issues as well, including three critical-severity weaknesses leading to code execution on the host. CVE-2026-123910 and CVE-2026-123911 (CVSS score of 9.8) are heap out-of-bounds write and use-after-free flaws in the I/O filter service, while CVE-2026-123912 (CVSS score of 9.3) is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the XHCI USB controller that requires local administrative privileges on a virtual machine. An attacker “may exploit this issue to execute code as the virtual machine’s VMX process running on the host. On ESX, the exploitation is contained within the VMX sandbox whereas, on Workstation and Fusion, this may lead to code execution on the machine where Workstation or Fusion is installed,” Broadcom explains.
